title: The Degenerate Mind of David Choe | Mini Documentary

segments.x: from the streets of LA to the halls of Facebook David Choe's journey is anything but ordinary the 47-year-old artist has made a name for himself with his raw Unapologetic style that pushes boundaries and challenges conventions forn Korean immigrants Cho dropped out of high school and found himself homeless and hitchhiking across the country but it was through ART that he

found his voice and his purpose armed to spray paint and a Fearless attitude he started tagging walls and creating gorilla style murals that caught the eye of the art World fast forward to today Cho's work has been exhibited in Galleries and Muse museums around the globe fetching Millions at auction but perhaps his most famous or inFAMOUS

Stroke of Luck came when he took stock instead of cash for painting murals at Facebook's first office that gamble would go on and make him one of the richest living artists love him or hate him there's no denying that David Choe is a true original a creative Force who refuses to play by the rules ch's

artistic talents were evident from a very young age as he had a natural gift for drawing despite that his journey into the art world was far from conventional to say the least he grappled with the troubled adolescence including brushes with the law and bounce of homelessness which profoundly shaped his worldview and artistic

expression Joe's breakthrough came in the late 1990s when he began gaining recognition for his distinctive graffiti art on the streets of Los Angeles his work characterized by bold colors intricate details and a raw Unapologetic energy quickly garnered attention and admiration however it was his unorthodox approach to art that truly set him apart

Joe embraced risk-taking and spontaneity often incorporating unconventional materials and techniques into his work he experimented with everything from spray paint and acrylics to blood and bodily fluids pushing the boundaries of artistic expression and challenging societal Norms early and often he would go out onto the streets of LA and tag up everything he can get his hands on one

of the things he became known for early on was painting whales all over walls it was a basic outline often accompanying phrases he traveled frequently at a young age as he took across country trip in an RV with some friends and decided then and there that's what he wanted to do with his life travel across the world

and see everything it has to offer this journey led him to the streets of Europe to as far as the jungles of Congo hitchiking rides and sleeping wherever he could CH begin submitting his illustrations to various companies like Rolling Stone Time Magazine and Newsweek hoping someone would pay him for his work but would ultimately get rejected

at the time he was also reading a lot of magazines and he noticed that they use a ton of illustrations as well he reached out to Hustler magazine and submitted his work to which they called him back and said they love it in 1996 Cho self-published a graphic novel titled slow jams which he made about 200 copies

of and gave away at ComicCon he went to numerous Publishers with the comic but Drew no interest a few years later in 1999 he submitted the book for the zerich grant and was awarded $5,000 to publish the second where he made about a th000 selling them for four bucks a pop after years of gaining no interest

Marvel Comics reached out to him and this is where he met one of his idols Jim Lee who is an artist for Marvel Comics and is currently the chief creative officer officer for DC Comics they green lit the project where Cho would create illustrations with X-Men characters doing R-rated stuff essentially but then got cancelled

without letting him know Cho upset wrote a profanity lace letter to the president of Marvel and it went crazy on the internet as he received a ton of backlash amongst the comic book Community around 2003 Cho would make his way to Japan to do art shows while there he would steal people's bikes and ride

around town tagging up the city one day he was in a convenience store and was about to steal a few items but last minute decided not to and put them down but it was too late as an undercover police officer saw him in the ACT Cho would punch the cop in the face and

booked it the officer pursued him until Cho was eventually caught by other officers he would get arrested and put into jail David was invited to Tokyo to create a mural and participate in a group art show while there he had a life-changing runin with the law I was running around doing all my

shopping and uh I guess undercover security guard had thought I had taken something in fact I just left it in the store and I I left and uh because of translation and misunderstandings you know he approached me in a very rough manner he slapped me upside my head and he was grabbing my bag of stuff that I

had bought and I was like is this guy really trying to mug me in front of all these people I was like all right man let go in my bag and he didn't do it you know he just his glasses broke cut his face his nose broke and he hit the wall on

the way down and then I just took off running I was scared I didn't know what to do and then just leave it alone for a while and then go go out and do something else David was arrested and thrown into jail as he awaited trial on assault and battery charges he was put into solitary

confinement he was put into solitary confinement for a brief period And while there he was allowed to have a few notebooks in those notebooks he started drawing all of his meals his career really took off after getting out of jail he started off by designing the commercials for the video game Need for

Speed underground to from there he designed an ad for Converse and then designed the album cover for Jay-Z and Lincoln Park's Collision Course a lot of his paintings he did while in jail started gaining attention as well people were fascinated by his creativity as he used soy sauce and urine for most of

these paintings one of the defining moments of Cho's career came in 2005 when he was commissioned by Facebook's founding president Shan Parker who was a fan of his work to paint murals at the company's headquarters he was offered one of two choices he could either take a one-time check of $60,000 in cash or

receive 0.25% of company stock an avid Gambler Cho chose the ladder a decision that would become incredibly lucrative when Facebook went public in 2012 Cho's shares were valued at over 200 million instantly making him one of the wealthiest artists in the world everyone was on Myspace everyone was like Facebook was like this it wasn't a joke

but it was like this Niche social media for college students and Shawn Parker with the Napster guy yeah Shawn Parker I I had met him right after after the Napster thing when they were trying to get sued for a trillion dollars he just was a fan of my art I had just gotten

out of prison in Japan and I owed everyone money he was like hey Dave Cho I told you one day I'm going to get a paying from you we got funding from um Peter at PayPal like he's like so what are you charging now and I'm like what do you want me to paint he's like I want

you to paint a mural on every single floor and I was like that's like multiple so I said 60 Grand and he's like okay he was like all right cool we can get you that and because I'm a gambler he goes or you could take stock people like oh he's so lucky but it's

cuz was degenerate during the 2010s is when he began to expand his online presence by making frequent appearances on Vice for an online series called thumbs up which had three seasons in total Cho and Harry Kim were filmed hitchhiking and Freight hopping from LA to Miami and Tijana to Alaska and then from Beijing to shenzen in 2013 Cho made

his first of many appearances on The Joe Rogan Experience and also started a lifestyle and entertainment podcast with adult film star Asa Akira titled DVDASA he also made an appearance on Anthony Bourdain's Parts unkknown on season 1 episode 2 Korea Town fast forward to 2021 he would create and release The Choe Show aired on FX where he essentially

takes the audience on a shared emotional experience painting portraits both literally and figuratively in 20123 he stared in the show beefs starring as Isaac Cho a sociopathic fun personality who jokes around a lot and isn't afraid to break the law one thing becomes abundantly clear in regards to Cho his story is as enigmatic and captivating as

the vibrant colors splashed across his canvases from his humble beginnings as a street artist to his rise to International Acclaim chose Unapologetic approach to creativity has left an indelible mark on the art world through interviews with friends collaborators and Cho himself we've glimpsed the complexities of his personality the demons he's battled and the triumphs he

celebrated from the streets of LA to the galleries of New York from the heights of success to the depths of uncertainty ch's journey is a testament to the power of art to transform lives and defy expectations
